trigger_phrase_or_event: copy locked in package before prompt/image handoff

copy_lock.copy:
This is the kind of love
I want us to grow into.

We will still get irritated
over keys, routes,
and very small things.

I will still say,
“Don’t talk to me.”

I hope you learn
when it means:
“Give me a minute.
Don’t go far.”

Not to fix it.
Just to notice
what it was really about.

And when the plan fails,
let’s still go on the date.
Even if it’s roadside chai.

He still checked the lock twice.
She still rolled her eyes.

Then she went back
and checked it with him.

agents.prompt_summary: Extract visual mechanics from references without copying frames, likenesses, or exact labels.
Prove every locked slide through concrete Aachu/Zuv behavior, not decorative illustration.
Define wants, hidden needs, eye-lines, hands, posture, distance, and joke-to-tenderness movement.
Plan readable text and brandmark placement independently for every request-locked native output.
Translate the selected visual system into specific final-generation and integrated-text constraints.
Select one system only after scoring copy alignment, relationship proof, visual variety, identity, aspect safety, and sendability.

visual_system_candidates.name: Slide-Led Evidence Plan
visual_system_candidates.case_for: Best preserves the locked copy while proving each beat through visible relationship behavior.
visual_system_candidates.risk: Must stay accountable to per-slide copy and avoid drifting into generic couple art.

visual_system_candidates.name: Format-First Label System
visual_system_candidates.case_for: Keeps the carousel visually legible and taggable when the concept depends on labels or a meme grammar.
visual_system_candidates.risk: Can become gimmicky if labels replace body language.

visual_system_candidates.name: Cinematic Romance Blocking
visual_system_candidates.case_for: Protects eye-lines, hands, distance, and emotional reversal.
visual_system_candidates.risk: Can become too soft or abstract if the hook needs deadpan specificity.

cross_debate: Keep the approved copy locked and make visuals do proof work.
Reject decorative quote-card scenes, generic couple stock poses, and repeated props.
Preserve the selected visual system unless visual-plan-quality records an explicit repair.
why_it_wins: Slide-Led Evidence Plan wins because it keeps the visual system accountable to the selected story arc.

slide_visual_blueprint.copy:
This is the kind of love
I want us to grow into.
slide_visual_blueprint.scene: FLASH-FORWARD COVER, one continuous physical scene. Rain-damp evening on a quieter service lane. Exactly Aachu and Zuv stand beside their single modest dark car, safely parked away from moving traffic. Across the divided road, a warmly lit restaurant entrance is visibly close but awkward to reach; it has no sign, letters, menu, staff, diners, silhouettes, or reflections. Beside the couple, a tiny roadside chai stall glows softly, also with no vendor and no signage. Aachu turns her gaze and chin toward the chai stall with a small conspiratorial half-smile. Zuv has just lowered the map phone and looks at her, understanding the pivot. Their bodies have begun angling toward the stall. The image must read without copy as: the original plan failed, but both are choosing a smaller date together. One umbrella is closed and leaning against the car; nobody holds it. No chai has been served yet. No scooter, motorbike, helmet, road sign, random lettering, or extra person.
slide_visual_blueprint.must_show: Visible Aachu/Zuv relationship behavior that proves the exact copy.

The same two people appear once in each intentional time vignette: four person depictions total, no fifth figure, no reflection people. The distance is enough to give her a minute but small enough to show he did not leave. The restaurant and chai stall are only faint geographic anchors. The face-down phone remains visibly on the dark car roof in the lower foreground. Zuv's head and gaze have turned away from the map and toward Aachu's face. He does not touch her or the phone. slide_visual_blueprint.scene: EARLIER CALLBACK TO BEFORE THE DATE, OUTSIDE THE APARTMENT ONLY. One premium storybook page with TWO SMALL UNFRAMED CHRONOLOGICAL VIGNETTES in the lower half, separated by open ivory paper and no hard divider. Both vignettes show the same apartment corridor from the OUTSIDE, the same fully closed wooden door, and the same couple in the exact date wardrobe. Door geometry is physically real and identical in both vignettes: hinges along the LEFT slab edge; a true RIGHT latch edge and jamb clearly visible; the lever spindle and lock hardware placed only a hand-width inboard from that RIGHT latch edge, never in the middle of the slab. Left vignette, first time beat: Zuv stands completely outside and tests the fully closed door by gently pulling the edge-mounted lever with his LEFT hand. Aachu has already walked three steps toward the visible lift, her feet and torso pointing away while her head rolls back with amused exasperation; she does not touch the door. Right vignette, second time beat: Aachu has visibly RETURNED and now stands beside Zuv at the same fully closed door. Zuv's LEFT hand still pulls the edge-mounted lever while Aachu's RIGHT palm presses the same door slab near the latch edge, so both participate in one shared push-pull check. Their small knowing smiles make the habit affectionate. The same two people appear once in each intentional time vignette: four person depictions total, no fifth figure. No footprints, arrows, indoor room, open door, middle-of-door lock, floating hardware, extra hands, door line through any body, corridor signage, apartment number, background person, scooter, or helmet.
